problem_class.label: convex
problem_class.details: Unconstrained minimization of convex components and their convex average; strong convexity is not required.
problem_class.evidence: LongTails/Setups/FiniteSumSmoothAndConvex.lean: spec.admissible, ConvexOn ℝ Set.univ for every component.

problem_class.label: finite_sum
problem_class.details: F(x) = (1/n) Σ_i f_i(x), with positive integer n.

oracle.label: exact_gradient
oracle.details: Replies are exact for every call index and oracle seed. There is no oracle error or sampling noise assumption.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/FiniteSumSmoothAndConvex.lean: spec.admissible, ∀ k seed i x, HasGradientAt.

oracle.label: component_gradient
oracle.details: Each query selects an index i and point x and returns the exact gradient ∇f_i(x). One selected component gradient counts as one oracle call.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/FiniteSumSmoothAndConvex.lean: spec.Query, spec.Reply, spec.admissible.HasGradientAt; LongTails/Template.lean: execute and Convergence.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: E is an arbitrary complete real inner-product space with a measurable-space structure; finite dimensionality is not required. Every component has globally L-Lipschitz gradient. A minimizer xstar exists with ‖x0−xstar‖≤R. E, n, L, R, ε and x0 are public; the component functions and minimizer are hidden. Valid parameters satisfy L>0, R≥0 and ε>0.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/FiniteSumSmoothAndConvex.lean: Params; spec.Public, publicInput, valid and admissible.

accuracy.label: objective_gap
accuracy.details: The output is a measurable E-valued point, its objective gap is integrable, and its expected gap from a global minimizer is at most ε. No particular iterate or averaging rule is required.

accuracy.label: expected
accuracy.details: E[F(output)−F(xstar)]≤ε under the product of algorithm and oracle seed laws, with a fixed oracle budget valid for every seed.

setup_category.label: classical
setup_category.reason: This is the standard smooth convex finite-sum component-gradient benchmark with expected objective accuracy, stated in a general real Hilbert space.
